title: MultipleTemporalLenses: compact temporal state survives, softmax lens routing does not
summary: Tests whether a fixed-size bank of heterogeneous temporal states can substitute for explicit history when the present query determines which age of the past matters. A residual-coordinate amendment corrects the original low-pass interpretation before the frozen gates. The main result is deliberately narrower than the motivating idea: compact multiscale state carries causally useful history, but query-softmax routing does not beat a generic query-conditioned reader, fails the same-present absolute-accuracy gate, and fails later-context reinterpretation. An explicit-history transformer solves the exact-anchor long stress while the 36-scalar compact models degrade sharply with age.

nodes.claim: Asks whether several fixed-size temporal summaries, exposed through query-conditioned readout, can provide useful age-selective access to history without storing an explicit token-by-token cache.
nodes.survived: Gate 2 shows that the compact state really carries usable history: raw+concat scores 0.5250 on same-present/different-history pairs versus 0.1207 after matched history shuffling, and residual-gated scores 0.4213 versus 0.1252. On the main held-out lag-shift task, raw+concat is the strongest compact reader at 0.5258 and beats the matched-state GRU and the repository's minimal selective-state control. Reader geometry matters: a generic query-conditioned concat reader is stronger than the tested softmax routing. The residual transform remains exactly invertible and exposes signed differences of overlapping low-pass states rather than pretending that slow filters are lag bins.
nodes.killed: The original 'query chooses a temporal lens' claim does not survive the frozen controls. Residual coordinates do not retain their development advantage on held-out lags; residual-gated is 0.4211 versus raw-gated 0.4430. The primary same-present criterion fails because residual-gated paired accuracy is only 0.4213, far below 0.75 despite a large shuffle effect. Later-context reinterpretation also fails: residual-gated reaches 0.4359 final accuracy with only +0.0018 context-consistent probability shift. On exact anchors (2,20,200), the tiny explicit-history transformer reaches 1.000 while the best compact model reaches 0.5461 overall and 0.2287 at lag 200. No cortical, dendritic, PAC, consciousness, or architecture-level superiority claim is established.
nodes.era: Compact temporal memory under adversarial controls

edges.why: MultipleTemporalLenses explicitly says it directly follows the TransformerToX / Rytmi line. It keeps TransformerToX's fixed-resident-state versus explicit-history comparison, then makes temporal coordinate basis and query/read geometry the object of frozen factorial and stress tests.

The repository explicitly carries forward the Rytmi/TransformerToX lesson that history being present in state is not enough: an invertibly related fast-minus-slow coordinate system can change what a current reader can use. MultipleTemporalLenses turns that observation into direct raw-versus-residual and gated-versus-concat tests.
